chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Furat, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in one of his speeches: 'Beware of ingratitude to the parents, for the aroma of Paradise is found from a travel distance of a thousand years, and it will not be found by the ungrateful one, nor by a severer of kinship ties, nor by an elderly adulterer, nor by one who drags his garment in pride. Indeed, greatness belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

key_terms.جَارُّ إِزَارِهِ: One who drags his garment (symbol of pride)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for being grateful to parents according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith links the spiritual reward of filial piety to the tangible sensory experience of Paradise, emphasizing that ingratitude (uquq) acts as a barrier to its scent. It expands the scope of exclusion to include those who sever kinship ties (qat' al-rahim) and the arrogant, clarifying that while humans may possess pride, ultimate 'greatness' (al-kibriya) is an exclusive attribute of Allah, a concept central to Shia theological understanding of divine majesty.
